records.text: Because Israel was an infant, I loved him, and out of Egypt I summoned his children.
As I summoned them, so they departed from My presence; they sacrificed to the Baalim and burned incense to carved images.
I bound Ephraim’s feet together; I took him up on My arm, but they did not know that I have healed them.
Amid human destruction I stretched them out in bonds of My love. I will be to them like a man slapping his cheeks; I will look toward him and be able to act for him.
Ephraim dwelt in Egypt, and Assur himself was his king, because he did not wish to return.
A sword grew weak in his cities and ceased in his hands, and they will eat from their schemes.
His people hang suspended from his dwelling, and God will be angry at his precious things and will certainly not exalt him.

How shall I deal with you, Ephraim? Shall I shield you, Israel? How shall I deal with you? Shall I make you like Adama and like Seboim? My heart turned within itself; My change of mind was stirred together.
I will certainly not act according to My furious anger; I will certainly not abandon Ephraim to be erased. For I am God and not a human being, holy within you, and I will not enter a city.
I will walk after the Lord. He will roar like a lion, because He Himself will howl, and children of waters will be astonished.
They will be astonished like a bird from Egypt and like a dove from the Assyrians’ land, and I will restore them to their houses, says the Lord.
Ephraim surrounded Me with falsehood, and Israel’s house and Judah with impieties. Now God knew them, and he will be called God’s holy people.
But Ephraim is an evil spirit; he pursued scorching heat all day, multiplied empty and worthless things, made a covenant with the Assyrians, and traded oil into Egypt.
The Lord has a case against Judah, to exact punishment on Jacob according to his ways; He will repay him according to his practices.
In the womb he tripped up his brother, and in his labors he prevailed against God
and prevailed with an angel and was able. They wept and entreated Me; in the house of On they found Me, and there he was spoken to.
The Lord God Almighty will be his memorial.
You will return in your God; keep mercy and judgment, and draw near to your God continually.
Canaan—in his hand is a balance of injustice; he loved to dominate.
Ephraim said, ‘Indeed I have become rich; I have found refreshment for myself.’ All his labors will not be found for him because of the injustices in which he sinned.
But I, the Lord your God, brought you up from Egypt’s land; I will still settle you in tents as on a festival day.
I will speak to prophets; I multiplied visions and was represented in likenesses through prophets.
If Gilead does not exist—then the rulers sacrificing at Gilgal were false, and their altars are like tortoises upon the field’s fallow ground.
Jacob withdrew to Syria’s plain; Israel served for a wife, and for a wife he kept guard.
Through a prophet the Lord brought Israel up from Egypt, and through a prophet he was preserved.
Ephraim provoked anger and exasperation; his blood will be poured upon him, and the Lord will repay him for his reproach.
According to Ephraim’s word, he received ordinances in Israel, assigned them to Baal and died.

He still continued to sin, and they made themselves a cast image from their silver according to the likeness of idols, works completed for them by craftsmen. They say, ‘Sacrifice human beings, for calves have run out!’
Therefore they will be like a morning cloud and like morning dew passing away, like chaff blown from a threshing floor and like vapor from locusts.

But I am the Lord your God, who establishes heaven and creates earth, whose hands created all heaven’s host. I did not display them to you so that you should follow them. I brought you up from Egypt’s land; you shall know no god except Me, and there is none who saves apart from Me.
I shepherded you in the wilderness, in an uninhabited land,
according to their pastures. They were filled to fullness, and their hearts were lifted up; for this reason they forgot Me.
I will be like a panther to them and like a leopard along the Assyrians’ road.
I will meet them like a bear in distress and tear open their heart’s enclosure. There forest lion cubs will devour them; field beasts will tear them apart.
In your destruction, Israel, who will help?
Where is this king of yours? Let him save you in all your cities; let him judge you, the one of whom you said, ‘Give me a king and a ruler.’
I gave you a king in My anger, and in My fury I held
a bundle of injustice. Ephraim—his sin is hidden.
Pangs like those of a woman giving birth will come upon him. This son of yours is not prudent, because he will certainly not endure amid the crushing of children.
I will rescue them from Hades’ hand and redeem them from death. Where is your punishment, Death? Where is your sting, Hades? Consolation is hidden from My eyes.

Because this one will make a division among brothers. The Lord will bring a scorching wind from the wilderness upon him and dry up his channels and desolate his springs; it will dry his land and all his desirable vessels.
Samaria will disappear because she opposed her God. They will fall by the sword; their nursing infants will be dashed to the ground, and their pregnant women will be ripped open.
Return, Israel, to the Lord your God, because you grew weak in your injustices.
Take words with you and return to the Lord your God. Speak to Him so that you do not receive injustice but receive good things, and we will repay the fruit of our lips.
Assur will certainly not save us; we will not mount a horse, and we will certainly no longer call the works of our hands “Our gods.” The One in you will have mercy on an orphan.
I will heal their dwellings; I will love them openly, because My anger turned away from them.
I will be like dew to Israel; he will blossom like a lily and put down his roots like Lebanon.
His branches will spread, and he will be like an olive tree laden with fruit; his fragrance will be like Lebanon.
They will return and settle beneath his shelter; they will live and be filled to intoxication with grain. His memorial will blossom like a vine, like Lebanon’s wine.
As for Ephraim, what has he still to do with idols? I humbled him, and I will strengthen him. I am like a thickly shading juniper; from Me your fruit is found.
Who is wise and will understand these things, or discerning and will recognize them? For the Lord’s ways are straight; the righteous will walk in them, but the impious will grow weak in them.
